challenge.better_approach: I looked at doing it on the PROVED side instead, with clearance accepting a refused hollow when another host's seal is green. That would leave the hollow unable to measure the teeth that can run here, and clearance would need a new 'refused but ok' state. Fixing the baseline is smaller: clearance's existing rules (a non-empty per-file list stands, an empty one reds hollow_file) already read the result correctly, so clearance does not change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a tooth UNRAN at HEAD is also UNRAN under every reversion, so excluding it from both readings is consistent. If a revert made a host-bound tooth suddenly run, it would show up as an extra green, never as a red, so it cannot fake load-bearing. Also, that the host-bound tooth's own coverage of the subject is vouched for by the other host's green seal on the same bytes. That seal shows the tooth passes there; it does not show the tooth reds on the revert. The named cost: on a Linux hollow, a subject that only the Windows tooth watches reads as hollow_file (empty list), which is loud and correct, never a silent pass.
challenge.prior_art: In-house: 50ac45cde4dd is the verdict's host_bound_reading (verdict.py:409-460), the same idea at the verdict door. 64ae0df3f1f3 is the tester writing no red when every failing tooth is UNRAN (device.py:969) and naming not_run_teeth. 7a275507818e is the verdict gate's host-bound disposal. None of them touches the hollow; grep for hollow tickets naming host-bound/UNRAN finds only those three plus 8c82. bfcb0d1cab45 (the hollow reverts a mode-only build) is a different class: it changes the revert set, not the baseline.
challenge.real_collision: None exclusive. Law 8 wants the reading to distinguish a hollow build, and the teeth that ran still do that. The 'every tooth ran at HEAD' rule in the baseline comment (a red about the proof, not about a file) is kept for teeth that RAN and failed. Only UNRAN is carved out, which is the distinction 64ae0df3f1f3 already draws for the seal.

answers.falsifier: A scratch proof with two declared teeth: A reads the subject file and runs on Linux, B prints UNRAN on Linux. Reverting the subject reds A, and the hollow seals the reading {subject: [A]} with B named unread on this host, rather than raising HollowUnmeasurable. With the subject reverted and A not depending on it, the reading is {subject: []}, which PROVED reds as hollow_file. A proof where both teeth print UNRAN still raises HollowUnmeasurable. A tooth that RAN and failed at HEAD still raises HollowUnmeasurable.
answers.from_idea: none, because the origin is a measured refusal, not an idea: cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py's HEAD baseline (lines 1190-1216) refused ticket 8c829d9b38b8 on 2026-11-23 with HollowUnmeasurable
answers.how: In hollow.py's HEAD baseline, subtract the proof record's evidence.not_run_teeth (the tester's own UNRAN reading, device.py:842, ticket 64ae0df3f1f3) from the missing set. Every later reading watches only the teeth that ran at HEAD. The seal names the teeth that went unread on this host, under a key outside the per-file reading. A proof where no declared tooth ran on this host still refuses, loudly, naming the host.
answers.traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured): a tooth this host did not run measured nothing, so reading it as red at HEAD is an unmeasured claim. Law 7: a diagnostic may not collapse 'not run here' into 'failed'. Law 8: the teeth that did run still have to red on the revert, so a hollow build still cannot pass.
answers.what: cairn test --hollow on a host that cannot run some of a proof's declared teeth reads those teeth as unread on this host, not as red at HEAD, and measures the reversion with the teeth that did run.

bullets.text: 8c82 and 3647 hold at PROVEME: the Linux hollow refuses because a Windows-only tooth reads UNRAN at HEAD and the baseline counts it as not green, so the teeth that ran never measure the revert.
The tester already knows which teeth did not run (evidence.not_run_teeth); the hollow throws it away one function later.

title: cairn test --hollow on a host that cannot run some of a proof's declared teeth reads those teeth as unread on this host,
